vasp.notes: Semiconductor bulk relaxation with ISIF=3 for full cell optimization. ISMEAR=0 (Gaussian) with small SIGMA=0.05 eV is appropriate for semiconductor relaxations. 8x8x8 Gamma-centered k-point mesh provides ~0.025 Å⁻¹ spacing (conventional cell). ENCUT=450 eV is well-converged for Si (ENMAX~250 eV). After relaxation completes, extract the optimized lattice constant from CONTCAR. The equilibrium lattice constant should be around 5.46-5.48 Å with PBE (experimental value is 5.431 Å). For production-quality convergence testing, verify with denser k-meshes (10x10x10 or 12x12x12) and check that energy changes are <1 meV/atom.

This is a bulk FCC Cu metal relaxation with full cell optimization (ISIF=3). Used ISMEAR=1 (Methfessel-Paxton) with SIGMA=0.1 eV appropriate for metals in both static and relaxation calculations. The 12×12×12 k-point mesh provides ~0.028 Å⁻¹ spacing, which should converge energies to ~1 meV/atom. After the calculation completes, check: (1) The entropy term T*S in OUTCAR should be <1 meV/atom to confirm adequate smearing convergence; (2) Extract the optimized lattice constant from the final cell vectors in CONTCAR; (3) The experimental Cu lattice constant is 3.615 Å - PBE typically underestimates by ~1-2%. If higher accuracy is needed, consider testing k-point convergence with 14×14×14 or 16×16×16 meshes.

MgO is a wide-gap insulator, so ISMEAR=0 (Gaussian smearing) with small SIGMA=0.05 is appropriate for the relaxation. ISIF=3 enables full cell relaxation (cell shape + volume + ions). ENCUT=520 eV is set above the typical O POTCAR ENMAX (~400 eV) by >1.3x for good convergence. 8x8x8 Gamma-centered k-mesh provides good convergence for this simple cubic rock-salt structure. After the calculation completes, the optimized lattice constant will be found in the final lattice vectors in CONTCAR. For MgO, the experimental lattice constant is ~4.21 Å, and PBE typically overestimates by ~1-2%. If more accurate energies are needed after relaxation, run a single-point calculation (NSW=0) with ISMEAR=-5 (tetrahedron method) using the relaxed CONTCAR geometry.

Diamond (C) is a wide-gap semiconductor, so ISMEAR=0 (Gaussian smearing) is appropriate. ENCUT=520 eV is chosen well above the recommended minimum for carbon (approximately 400 eV for light elements) to ensure accurate forces and stress tensor during full cell relaxation. ISIF=3 allows optimization of both cell shape/volume and ionic positions. EDIFFG=-0.005 eV/Å gives tight force convergence for accurate lattice constant determination. The 11×11×11 Gamma-centered k-point mesh provides good convergence for the small cubic cell (approximately 0.025 Å⁻¹ spacing). After the calculation completes, the optimized lattice constant can be extracted from the final lattice vectors in CONTCAR. You will need to generate the POTCAR file by concatenating the C POTCAR from your potpaw_PBE directory.
